newsitem.title: TURKEY: German Grundig eyes bigger share in Turkish market.
newsitem.headline: German Grundig eyes bigger share in Turkish market.

text.p: German consumer electronics, audio and video producer Grundig targets a major share in sales of imported TV sets and audio equipment in Turkey by setting up a new partnership with the local Mercansoy group, a senior company official said.

"In the first year of our (company's) second phase in Turkey, beginning from October 1, our aim is to reach a one digit percentage share in the market," Fred Hamann, general manager of Grundig International, told a press conference on Tuesday.
The Grundig brand entered the Turkish market in the 1970's with local Cihan Elektronik as the main distributor and later producer.
"But during 1980's our Turkish partner had serious financial problems and even our support could not help them," Hamann said.
He said the advantages of Turkey's customs union with the European Community which took effect in January, would help them to start importing Grundig equipments produced in Germany and Austria.

"Production in Turkey may be taken into consideration after achieving a reasonable market share," Hamann said, adding that their criteria would be a 100,000 unit sale corresponding to a 10 percent annual market share and a reasonable export figure.

In answer to a question on the former partner Cihan's production of Grundig brands, Hamann said: "We will not let two different Grundig brands in Turkey. We will take the necessary measures to stop Cihan Elektronik's production of Grundig brands because their licence accord has been abolished."
Hamann also said Grundig and its 32 percent owner Phillips would be complementaries rather than competitors in the Turkish market.

Domestic partner Mercansoy, a group established in 1957 as a carpet and furniture retailer, switched to durables marketing and distributing business in the 1980's, including Grundig brand audio and video equipments.
